transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Xu (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (Polaris Head of Partnerships), Maya Singh (Polaris Cloud PM), Evan Rivera (Polaris DevOps), Olga Petrov (Polaris Security)

Summary:
Partner technical sync to align on Redwood marketplace listing steps, reference architecture for Polaris managed offering, and joint solution packaging. Discussed security artifacts, packaging (Helm/Terraform), billing integration, and timeline for pilot and listing approval.

Topics:
- Marketplace listing requirements and assets
- Reference architecture (VPC, VPC peering, private control plane, KMS)
- Joint solution deliverables: Helm chart, Terraform module, test plan
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS/HSM
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we will run through marketplace listing, a reference arch, and the joint solution plan. Lina and I will lead the tech bits.
[00:18] Jared: Thanks Samir. We are excited to get the listing live and make sure the reference arch maps to our managed offering. Quick context, we want the marketplace SKU to support metered billing and a reserved tier.
[00:30] Lina: Cool. Quick question on metering - Redwood supports per-token and embedding units; for marketplace we typically map to either usage-based or monthly commit. We can include both in the listing, but the billing adapter needs the metering events.
[00:47] Maya: So we will need an event spec for billing. Evan, does your billing team support webhook metering?
[00:53] Evan: Yes we have a usage ingestion pipeline. We'll need docs for the event schema and authentication. Ideally can be signed payloads or JWT.
[01:05] Samir: Great, Lina will share the billing event spec. Also note some marketplaces require a trial SKU and first 30-day credits, we can support that.
[01:18] Olga: On security, SOC2 and encryption at rest matter a lot. Do you have a template for the SOC2 report redacted and a list of encryption algorithms?
[01:28] Lina: We can provide a SOC2 redacted report and our KMS integration guide. For private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and Terra-formable key rotation patterns.
[01:36] Jared: For the reference arch, we need to show VPC peering options vs private control plane. Customers will ask, can we run in our VPC with a private control plane?
[01:45] Samir: Yes, Redwood Private offers both: VPC connectors for control plane and an on-prem package for air-gapped. The reference arch doc should show both flows. Lina, we talked about diagrams - can you capture both patterns?
[01:55] Lina: Yep, I'll produce two diagrams: 1) VPC peering with public control plane endpoints restricted by CIDR and 2) customer VPC with private control plane / private link.
[02:05] Evan: On networking, do you support direct VPC peering or only transit via NAT? We prefer peering for lower latency.
[02:12] Lina: We support both; peering is recommended for lower latency. Note that marketplace listing sometimes forces public endpoints for billing callbacks, so we'll note the pattern for secure callbacks via private link or signed webhooks.
[02:25] Jared: About packaging - Polaris wants a turnkey deployment: helm chart + terraform module + sample app. What do you expect Redwood to provide vs Polaris?
[02:33] Samir: Redwood will provide a reference Helm chart, sample values, and a terraform module for creating the runtime resources in common clouds. Polaris will provide the container image, an ingress cert, and CI steps.
[02:44] Maya: For the container image we need to know recommended base images and any required startup flags for KV cache warmup, etc.
[02:50] Lina: We'll add recommended base images to the repo and note runtime flags. Also include quantization profile recommendations if you're using smaller instances.
[02:59] Evan: Good, we will share registry access. Also, on autoscaling: does Redwood dedicated support burst capacity? We may want predictable throughput with bursts.
[03:08] Samir: Yes, dedicated supports reserved capacity + burst policies. We'll document SLOs and throughput per GPU type in the listing.
[03:16] Olga: A couple security questions - SAML SSO, RBAC mapping to customer groups, audit logs retention and export.
[03:25] Lina: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with roles mapping to groups. Audit logs can be exported to customer S3 or pushed to SIEM via webhook. Retention can be configured per account.
[03:37] Olga: Also, KMS key custody: can keys reside in our KMS? We need customer-managed keys.
[03:43] Samir: Yes, customer-managed KMS supported; we have a KMS integration guide. For HSM-backed keys we do an ops checklist for key rotation.
[03:52] Jared: For the marketplace listing itself, what assets do you need? Screenshots, logos, description, pricing, trial rules, technical support level, and an onboarding doc?
[04:02] Lina: Exactly: listing title, short/long description, logos at specified sizes, 1-2 screenshots, pricing tiers, trial policy, support SLA, and a short onboarding doc or quickstart. Also a partner contact email and support URL.
[04:15] Jared: Are there any gotchas - e.g., tech review by marketplace that rejects private endpoint patterns?
[04:22] Samir: Sometimes marketplaces have restrictions on private networking. We will flag the alternative public-backed flow and include a security section that explains private/control plane deployment as an enterprise offering, and marketplace listing can reference the enterprise contact.
[04:36] Maya: On timeline, Polaris wants listing live within 3 weeks if possible to coincide with their Q2 partner push. Is that realistic?
[04:44] Samir: 3 weeks is tight but doable if artifacts are provided quickly. Lina assumes 5 workdays to prepare reference charts and diagram once we have container access. Marketplace approval can be variable - typically 7-14 days.
[04:58] Evan: We'll aim to provide images and terraform bits within 4 business days.
[05:04] Lina: I'll also prepare a compatibility matrix of supported GPU instance types and recommended batch sizes to put into the listing.
[05:12] Samir: Good to include cost/perf notes - customers always ask about tokens per second and cost per 1k tokens on each profile.
[05:21] Jared: For the joint solution, Polaris wants co-branded quickstart and a reference demo. Can Redwood produce a demo script and small sample app?
[05:29] Lina: Yes, we have reference apps. We'll provide a sample repo and a demo script. We can co-brand it.
[05:35] Olga: Any compliance paperwork needed for listing? Some marketplaces require a security questionnaire.
[05:41] Samir: We'll provide the vendor security questionnaire and the SOC2 redacted report. Lina, do you have the questionnaire link?
[05:47] Lina: I'll attach a standard security questionnaire template and point to the compliance page.
[05:52] Jared: Great. One more thing - telemetry and logging for the joint solution. Polaris wants a dashboard for per-tenant latency and cost. Is that available?
[06:01] Samir: Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. For joint customers we can surface a dashboard with tenant filters. We'll include screenshots in the listing assets.
[06:14] Evan: We'll need APIs for pulling usage data into our billing system.
[06:18] Lina: We expose usage APIs and can set push or pull. We'll share the API spec.
[06:24] Jared: Ok, sounds good. Let's capture the immediate deliverables.
[06:29] Samir: Quick recap of owners: Samir will send partner onboarding deck and pricing guidance; Lina will produce the reference arch diagram, helm chart stub, and API specs; Evan will hand over registry access and terraform bits; Olga will provide SOC2 scope confirmation.
[06:44] Maya: I'll coordinate internal legal for marketplace terms.
[06:48] Samir: Great. Any other questions?
[06:51] Evan: One small technical point - for KV cache prewarm, are there startup endpoints we need to hit or is it automatic?
[06:58] Lina: There is a warm-up endpoint for pre-loading model weights and KV cache; we'll include it in the helm hooks.
[07:05] Jared: Perfect. If there are no other blockers we can close and execute on the action items.
[07:11] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the checklist and links.
[07:16] Lina: I'll upload a draft reference arch doc to the partner repo and ping the group.
[07:20] Jared: Thank you, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Recap / Next steps (as discussed):
- Redwood to provide marketplace checklist, SOC2 redacted report, billing event spec, reference architecture diagrams, helm chart stub, and API spec.
- Polaris to provide container image, registry access, terraform module, and legal coordination for marketplace terms.
- Schedule joint PRD review: 2026-04-30.

References mentioned: partner onboarding deck (link to be shared), compliance questionnaire (link), sample repo (link), marketplace asset template (link). Some transcribed words may be imperfect (K V cache, aurracloud etc).
